items.summary: Python code that reproduces all results, figures and supporting tables of Dixit, AchutaRao and Sandeep, "Future Warming Shortens the Memory of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and Erodes a Source of Near-Term Predictability" (submitted to Earth's Future). The analysis uses eleven CMIP6 models (piControl, historical, SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5), the CESM2 and MIROC6 large ensembles and ERSSTv5, regridded to the 2-degree ERSSTv5 grid. items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.

items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

items.summary: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.
items.title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition

items.summary: EHR2Trace converts local hospital EHR extracts (delimited text and spreadsheets) into OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS. items.summary: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. We propose PRB-WM, a physics-regularized Beta world model for predictive per-subcarrier link adaptation on real time-varying UWA channels. A persistence-anchored stochastic latent-space dynamics model learns how the channel evolves; a counterfactual outcome head evaluates, for every candidate modulation and coding scheme (MCS), a Beta-binomial distribution of bit errors on shared imagined futures; and a chance-constrained receding-horizon model predictive controller maximizes expected spectral efficiency subject to a bounded probability of violating the bit error rate (BER) target. To the best of our knowledge, PRB-WM is the first world model for UWA communications. In closed-loop replay of six measured sea-trial links from the public UWA Channel Library against a 24-method pool spanning the full methodological spectrum, PRB-WM attains a mean goodput 87% above the strongest baseline, ranks first on all six time-varying links at the longest lookahead, and is the only method whose realized frame risk decreases systematically with lookahead, meeting the BER-violation contract where no baseline does. Ablations confirm that rollout sampling dispersion is essential to the chance constraint and that the physics anchor is necessary for trainability.
items.title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels

items.summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. Run or export the pipeline from Dockstore Dockstore is a GA4GH compliant open platform for sharing Docker-based tools like WDL workflows. You can find WARP pipelines in Dockstore and run them on the Dockstore platform or export them to other platforms (including Terra). To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. items.summary: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance is a practical research and educational resource for documenting and governing generative-AI-assisted social-science research. The resource develops a workflow for distinguishing AI-assisted proposal generation, researcher evaluation and governance, local empirical execution, adversarial challenge, manuscript revision and reason provenance. It includes reusable templates, completed worked examples drawn from the PISA research programme, guidance on claim preservation and manuscript governance, and public-release screening materials. The resource is intended to support transparent attribution and disciplined research practice rather than to prescribe a universal workflow or to provide evidence that AI-assisted research is inherently superior to human-only research.

items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can participate in producing educational research data as well as analysing them. This dual role creates opportunities for studying intellectual activity while complicating the relationship between observation and intervention. This conceptual article connects two research routes: analysis of existing narrative documents and study of trajectories produced through human–AI interaction. A selective historical genealogy links scientific photography, personal documents, concept mapping and verbal protocols to contemporary hybrid intelligence and learning analytics. Observable cognition denotes recorded manifestations of intellectual activity, interpreted under explicit conditions. Multiscale narrative analysis connects events, episodes, trajectories and corpora through within-case interpretation, cross-case comparison and return to original evidence. The central proposal is to preserve a revisable link between each cross-case claim, its supporting episodes, the provenance of contributions and evidence that could challenge the interpretation. The framework extends from conversational generative interaction to increasingly agentic configurations, in which greater trace granularity also increases the need to attribute operations to the human participant, the system, or distributed activity between them. The framework specifies data units, audit procedures and four propositions for empirical evaluation. A fictional educational design episode illustrates how the same revision can support competing explanations. The proposed tests separate the informational value of process records from claims about learning gains, and assess whether assisted analysis preserves consequential context at an acceptable cost. The framework integrates established methods into an assessable research design; its feasibility and comparative advantage remain to be demonstrated. -------- Preprint v1.0. This version has not undergone peer review.
items.title: From tacit knowledge to observable cognition: A framework for tracing interaction with AI and analysing educational narratives across scales

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.
items.title: Inverse Radius Kernel and Optical Phase Registration

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.

This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. items.summary: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.
items.title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition

items.summary: The Mathematics of 3D Printing Slicing: STL Geometry, Ray-Casting & Toolpaths is an open-access engineering monograph and interactive instructional module published by the Prep4Uni.Online OER Initiative . This work provides an analytical, undergraduate/postgraduate-level treatment of the computational geometry foundations required to translate three-dimensional surface meshes into layer-by-layer machine toolpaths. Aligned with international accreditation standards—specifically the Washington Accord (WA1–WA5) and EUR-ACE First/Second Cycle frameworks—this publication establishes the mathematical proofs, vector algorithms, and point-in-polygon logic governing modern additive manufacturing slicing software. Core Mathematical & Computational Themes: STL Topology & Facet Representation: Analysis of unstructured triangulated surface meshes, outward unit normal vectors (\(\mathbf{n}\)), vertex coordinate systems, and planar boundary extraction. Parametric Facet-Plane Intersection: Step-by-step vector linear interpolation for deriving the intersection segment \(S_k\) formed by cutting planes at \(z = z_k\), addressing non-manifold edges, vertex touching, and numerical epsilon shifts. Jordan Curve Theorem & Parity Logic: Formal implementation of the 2D Ray-Casting algorithm and Even-Odd Parity test for robust interior, exterior, and internal void classification across arbitrary closed slices. Toolpath Trajectory Generation: Comparative kinematics and geometry between continuous concentric perimeter offset loops and 45° zigzag parallel hatch raster patterns. Formative Assessment Suite: A three-tier verification suite comprising 8 foundational concepts, 7 real-world slicer failure debugging scenarios, and 6 step-by-step quantitative engineering worked examples. items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.
items.title: Fisher information metric tensors for 'Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information'

items.summary: NANOROBOTIC CARGO TRANSPORT AND MICROSCALE MANIPULATION INTEGRITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation DOI Fission Research Flagship 02 | Starli Active Nanosystems Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli | Research Atlas v1.0 (October 2026) How can a micro/nanorobotic carrier demonstrate that the object arriving at a designated target is the same intact cargo that was originally loaded, that it was completely and correctly released, and that the carrier or its residues have been accounted for? This English-language research atlas converts cargo-delivery and micromanipulation demonstrations into a falsifiable end-to-end mission-integrity problem. The research develops a five-layer architecture for source identity and material tolerance, microscale contact mechanics, independently observable mission-state transitions, adversarial fault injection, and blind cross-platform requalification. Thirty mathematically distinct derivation stations connect probabilistic joint-task qualification to chemical mass balance, optical-label dissociation, surface adsorption, force-dependent detachment, microcontact mechanics, drag, kinetic release, spatial uncertainty, carryover contamination, whole-facility energy accounting, missing-fate bounds and hard safety vetoes. Eighty-two chapters each have a dedicated core-equation opening and five separate research sections. Two hundred Research Gates propose independent comparisons, physical perturbations, competing explanations, measurable failure criteria and reproducibility artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate systems that future investigators are invited to overturn, repair or rebuild. A machine-readable research atlas and formula-gate-DOI index enable AI-assisted comparison and future research reuse. The central endpoint is a correlated joint event: correct cargo identity and integrity, correct target, independently confirmed release, and verified carrier retrieval or authorized terminal disposition. The manuscript insists on counting every initiated mission rather than multiplying attractive substep success rates. It also distinguishes visible fluorescence from chemically intact cargo, externally actuated manipulation from on-board autonomy, and destination arrival from complete task closure. Strong benchmarks include optical tweezers, established magnetic-bead handling, microfluidic conveyance and conventional microgrippers under matched task difficulty, time and whole-facility energy use. Research status: This is a hypothesis-generating, nonclinical experimental-design atlas; it reports no newly conducted cargo experiments, clinical performance or proven integrated device. Foundational and recent DOI-identified publications provide engineering context but do not validate its new claims. The 200 Gates are open problems, not accomplished results. The actual text length and layout follow the substance of individual chapters rather than an artificially enforced 100,000-word count. items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. items.summary: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. We propose PRB-WM, a physics-regularized Beta world model for predictive per-subcarrier link adaptation on real time-varying UWA channels. A persistence-anchored stochastic latent-space dynamics model learns how the channel evolves; a counterfactual outcome head evaluates, for every candidate modulation and coding scheme (MCS), a Beta-binomial distribution of bit errors on shared imagined futures; and a chance-constrained receding-horizon model predictive controller maximizes expected spectral efficiency subject to a bounded probability of violating the bit error rate (BER) target. To the best of our knowledge, PRB-WM is the first world model for UWA communications. In closed-loop replay of six measured sea-trial links from the public UWA Channel Library against a 24-method pool spanning the full methodological spectrum, PRB-WM attains a mean goodput 87% above the strongest baseline, ranks first on all six time-varying links at the longest lookahead, and is the only method whose realized frame risk decreases systematically with lookahead, meeting the BER-violation contract where no baseline does. Ablations confirm that rollout sampling dispersion is essential to the chance constraint and that the physics anchor is necessary for trainability.
items.title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels

items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

items.summary: This replication package contains the experimental artifacts, anonymized empirical benchmark dataset (N = 5,000 paired student-opportunity records), statistical verification scripts, database definitions, and microservices source code for the research paper: "Hybrid Vector-Temporal Matching for Student Freelance Placement: An Empirical Study of Database-Level Vector Offloading" Targeted for Information and Software Technology (IST, Elsevier). Package Contents: data/: Anonymized benchmark dataset (students_data_tesis_final.csv) featuring 168-hour weekly availability matrices and raw ablation output. benchmarks/: Automated Python scripts for Stratified 5-fold cross-validation ablation (C1 to C4), Wilcoxon Signed-Rank hypothesis testing, Cliff's Delta effect size calculation, and bootstrap confidence intervals. database/: PostgreSQL 16 schema and stored procedure definitions for HNSW Approximate Nearest Neighbor vector search (pgvector) and dynamic schedule intersection. turborepo-src/: Clean source code of the decoupled microservices monorepo (API Gateway, Matching Service, ML Engine, and shared Protocol Buffers). System Requirements: Python 3.10+ with NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, and NLTK. Node.js v20+ / pnpm v9+ and Docker Engine for microservice orchestration.

items.summary: Python code that reproduces all results, figures and supporting tables of Dixit, AchutaRao and Sandeep, "Future Warming Shortens the Memory of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and Erodes a Source of Near-Term Predictability" (submitted to Earth's Future). "bash run_all.sh" runs the full analysis. The folder results/ contains the outputs used in the paper, from which most figures can be redrawn without the model data. See README.md for requirements, input data layout and the mapping of scripts to sections, figures and tables.
